lines.text: A tiny network makes a guess. The guess is wrong.
Three clay workers stand in a line. Each one takes a number, changes it a little, and passes it on.
At the end, a judge compares the answer with the truth, and measures how wrong it was. That is the loss.
Now the blame goes backwards. The last worker asks: how much of this error was my fault?
Then it tells the worker before it, who asks the same question, and passes it on.
Each worker gets a share of the blame. Big share, big nudge. Small share, small nudge.
Every worker turns its dial a little, in the direction that makes the error smaller.
Do it again with the next example. Do it millions of times, and the guesses get better.
